title: Logrolling and Trade-offs
description: Find what each side cares about least, and trade on it.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Logrolling is trading across issues: you give ground on something you value little and gain something you value a lot, and the other side does the reverse. Both end up better off than if they had split every issue down the middle.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Different sides weight issues differently. By trading on those differences rather than compromising on each, the deal can create value instead of merely dividing it.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: You concede on the payment date to keep the price; they concede on price to keep the date.
One side gives up a small item to secure a bigger priority elsewhere.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Multiple issues on the table at once.
Exchanges across issues rather than haggling on one number.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Put several issues on the table, learn each side's priorities, then trade where your priorities differ most.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: A single-issue negotiation where no trade is possible.
Pretending to care about something only to trade it away.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Keep several issues open so trades are possible.
Ask what matters most to them before revealing what matters most to you.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Negotiating one issue at a time.
Splitting every difference instead of trading.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: More issues means more room to create value.
Do not reveal your priorities too early.
